contracts.title: Durham County Council are looking for providers to work in partnership to develop a bespoke residential home within the boundaries of County Durham or surrounding areas for an identified young person.
contracts.description:
To open up discussion with providers about the development of 'new' registered children's home provision in County Durham or in the surrounding area to meet the specific needs of the young person. The home is for one young person initially, with the flexibility to move in a second young person at a later date, subject to a positive matching exercise. 

A provider may already have a registered children's home with a highly experienced registered manager and are able to develop a smaller satellite home (in accordance with new Ofsted guidance for registering a multi building children's home). 

Provider's that have knowledge and experience of working with children with complex needs and within Ofsted's Regulatory Framework. 

Providers that have a track record of achieving positive outcomes for children / young people, who provide consistent good quality care and who demonstrate stickability. 


What we will offer as a Local Authority: 

Tailored multi-agency planning about the additional support and resources that can be offered in line with the needs of the child. 

A dedicated point of contact for advice when setting up a home in Durham. 

A letter of support for the change of use planning process. 

A dedicated point of contact when the home is operational. 

Linkages with the virtual school to ensure that children are able to access suitable education provision in line with their individual needs. 

Access to an advocacy and independent visitor services.

contracts.title: Contract for Civil Parking Enforcement and Management Services for Durham County Council
contracts.description:
The contract is for the provision of Civil Parking Enforcement and Management Services ("the Contract") to Durham County Council.

Durham County Council is seeking a single service provider to assist with the delivery of a variety of parking services throughout County Durham. These services include the operation of a Parking Shop, Civil Parking Enforcement, the consideration of challenges up to Notice to Owner stage, permit administration, on & off street pay and display machine maintenance, cash collection, banking and Park and Ride car park management.The Council intends to invite the 5 highest SQ scoring bidders to tender, subject to having passed Part 1, Part 2, and the other sections of Part 3, and achieved a minimum weighted score of 65% for the Technical Questions.  The Contract duration is 5.5 years with an option to extend entirely at the Council's discretion for a further 5 years. 

At the end of the initial 5.5 years period the Council will determine whether to grant an additional 5-year extension. Any Extension will be discussed relevant to the potential review of equipment and necessary replacement as required.

contracts.title: County Durham Growth Fund Due Diligence Services
contracts.description:
This contract is for Due Diligence Services for the County Durham Growth Fund (CDGF).

The County Durham Growth Fund is a new grant programme for SMEs in County Durham for capital investment projects to stimulate and enable sustainable business growth, and is funded by the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF) as part of the 2014-2020 European Structural and Investment Fund Programme.

This external due diligence service is being procured for Business Durham, the economic development organisation for Durham County Council, who will be delivering the County Durham Growth Fund in partnership with BE Group.

The successful contractor will provide due diligence support to Business Durham and BE Group on grant applications submitted to BE Group, by qualifying SMES and approved in principle by the investment panel, including (but not limited to) preparation of reports with recommendations covering eligibility of expenditure, viability, deliverability, management capability and State Aid compliance.

The project will be delivered on behalf of Durham County Council.

contracts.title: Durham County Council Contract for Mobile Sexual Health Service
contracts.description:
To provide Mobile Sexual Health Service in County Durham.

Within County Durham, the overall aim of the service is to increase and widen access to SRE and sexual health services for young people aged 13-19 years in order to reduce the risk of unwanted conceptions and of contracting STIs.   

Provider to deliver a Mobile Sexual Health Service, operating at targeted locations within County Durham: youth & community settings; colleges; schools; & other locations e.g. skate parks or fast food restaurant car parks, within teenage pregnancy ‘hot spot’ areas. 

Provider to supply/maintain any vehicles used to provide service, (responsible for vehicle taxation, insurance, repairs, maintenance, driver licence checks/qualifications, liable for any driver infringements and car parking charges).

Providing sexual health services including C-Card and chlamydia screening and refer to Contraception and Sexual Health (CASH) services.  Deliver a Sex and Relationship Education programme.  A minimum of two suitably qualified youth workers to deliver sessions.

Provider must deliver a minimum of four sexual health sessions per week, each lasting three hours, over 42 weeks of year (i.e. excluding school holiday periods).  During these sessions, the Mobile Sexual Health Service may be delivered at two or three different locations within a specific area (usually evenings and weekends). 

To work with local services/agencies e.g. schools, Durham Constabulary, the One Point Service, school nursing service and local Health staff.  Attend multi-agency meetings and take part in multi-agency health events.  Utilise a suitable Information Management and Technology software system that will support data collection/reporting and the secure storage of confidential service user notes.  Collect quality and performance monitoring data according to Durham County Council requirements and submit this in accordance with agreed timescales.

contracts.title: Dry Recyclables for Durham County Council
contracts.description:
In 2012 Durham County Council introduced Alternate Weekly Collection arrangements. As a result the majority of households in the County now receive a fortnightly recycling collection. Households have been issued with a 240 litre wheeled bin for mixed dry recyclable material along with a separate container for mixed glass. Details of the materials which are targeted for collection can be found at: ://www.durham.gov.uk/whatgoeswhere .
The Council currently has no plans to make any significant changes to its waste and recycling collection arrangements
The Council is now seeking expressions of interest for the provision of dry recyclable processing services.
The primary objective of this contract is for the successful bidder(s) to maximise the recycling rate for material collected by the Council through its household and trade waste recycling collections and to maximise diversion from landfill.
Bidders will be required to have a delivery point for receipt of the contract waste within 75 miles from a central point nominated by the Council for each Lot. The Council will deliver the dry recyclable waste to the successful bidder(s), no haulage services are required as part of this contract.
 At tender stage the Council will be inviting bids based on either payment made by the contractor to the Council OR payment made by the Council to the contractor OR a combination of both therefore the Council is, at this stage of the procurement, unable to give an estimated value for the contract(s)
 It is anticipated that the total tonnage of mixed dry recyclables and mixed glass to be accepted and processed each year will be 51,000 tonnes. However these are approximate quantities. The Council is offering bidders the opportunity to submit proposals for the following Lots:
  Lot 1: 20,000 tonnes (20 ktpa);
  Lot 2: 12,000 tonnes (12 ktpa);
  Lot 3: 19,000 tonnes (19 ktpa) or 
  Lot 4: 51,000 tonnes (51 ktpa) (overall tonnage)
